title: Passive Voice: All Tenses + Get Passive
grammarTitle: Passive Voice — Complete Tense Review + Get Passive
grammarNote: На уровне B1 вы должны уметь использовать пассивный залог во ВСЕХ временах свободно. Кроме того, важно понимать "get passive" — альтернативный способ образования пассива с get, который подчёркивает опыт субъекта, часто с оттенком неожиданности или незапланированности.

grammarTable.subject: Present Simple
grammarTable.example: "Results are published every Monday." / "Samples are collected at dawn."

grammarTable.subject: Present Continuous
grammarTable.example: "The project is being assessed." / "Three vendors are being evaluated."

grammarTable.subject: Present Perfect
grammarTable.example: "The proposal has been approved." / "The budget has been allocated."

grammarTable.subject: Past Simple
grammarTable.example: "The system was introduced six years ago." / "The data was collected carefully."

grammarTable.subject: Past Continuous
grammarTable.example: "The samples were being processed when the error was found."

grammarTable.subject: Past Perfect
grammarTable.example: "The policy had been reviewed before the meeting." / "Bacteria had been killed."

grammarTable.subject: Future (will)
grammarTable.example: "The results will be published next week." / "Changes will be implemented."

grammarTable.subject: Modal passive
grammarTable.example: "Errors must be corrected." / "Issues should be raised." / "It can be fixed."

grammarTable.subject: GET passive
grammarTable.example: "The system got broken." / "The deal got done." / "He's getting promoted."

rows.form: GET (present) + pp
rows.example: "She gets paid at the end of the month." / "Problems get noticed eventually." ✅

rows.form: GOT (past) + pp
rows.example: "He got arrested." / "The meeting got cancelled." / "She got promoted last year." ✅

rows.form: IS/ARE GETTING (present continuous)
rows.example: "He's getting treated at the hospital." / "The system is getting fixed." ✅

rows.form: WILL GET + pp (future)
rows.example: "You'll get paid on Friday." / "The issue will get resolved." ✅

rows.form: GET emphasises subject's experience
rows.example: "She got fired" = more emphasis on her experience than "She was fired." ✅

rows.form: GET NOT used in formal/academic
rows.example: Avoid "get passive" in academic essays, formal reports. Use "be passive" instead. ✅

grammarExtra.title: Choosing between active and passive: decision guide

rows.form: USE PASSIVE when agent is obvious/unimportant
rows.example: "The road was repaired last week." (Of course workers repaired it.) ✅

rows.form: USE PASSIVE when agent is unknown
rows.example: "My phone was stolen." (We don't know who stole it.) ✅

rows.form: USE PASSIVE to focus on result or process
rows.example: "The data was collected and analysed over three months." (Focus on process.) ✅

rows.form: INCLUDE BY + agent when it adds value
rows.example: "The theory was proposed by Darwin." (Darwin = important, worth naming.) ✅

rows.form: OMIT by + agent when obvious
rows.example: "The parliament passed the law." ✅ (obvious agent — no need to say "by members of parliament")

rows.form: AVOID passive for personal, narrative writing
rows.example: In personal essays or narratives: active is usually more natural. ✅

grammarExtra.title: By + agent — when to include it

rows.form: Include when agent is surprising/interesting
rows.example: "The building was designed BY A STUDENT." (Surprising! Worth mentioning.) ✅

rows.form: Include when agent is the focus
rows.example: "The theory of relativity was developed BY EINSTEIN." (Einstein = crucial.) ✅

rows.form: Omit when agent is obvious or irrelevant
rows.example: "The road was repaired." (Obviously by workers — no need to say.) ✅

rows.form: Omit when agent is unknown
rows.example: "My car was scratched." (Unknown agent — "by someone" = unnecessary.) ✅

rows.form: Omit in process descriptions
rows.example: "The data was collected, processed, and analysed." (In science, no "by researchers" needed.) ✅

grammarExtra.title: ❌ Common passive errors at B1 level

rows.form: ✗ "The report was wrote by him."
rows.example: ✅ "The report was WRITTEN by him." — past PARTICIPLE, not past simple! ✅

rows.form: ✗ "She is being promoted by the company."
rows.example: ✅ "She is being promoted." — when agent obvious, omit "by the company." ✅

rows.form: ✗ "It was being understood."
rows.example: ✅ Stative verbs (understand, know, like) cannot be passive Continuous. "It was understood." ✅

rows.form: ✗ "The samples has been collected."
rows.example: ✅ "The SAMPLES have been collected." — plural subject → HAVE, not has. ✅

rows.form: ✗ Using get passive in formal writing
rows.example: ✅ In academic essays: "The candidate was selected" NOT "got selected." ✅

grammarExtra.title: Passive tenses in context: a connected sequence

rows.form: The problem WAS IDENTIFIED last year.
rows.example: Past Simple Passive — when something happened.

rows.form: Since then, solutions HAVE BEEN PROPOSED.
rows.example: Present Perfect Passive — up to now.

rows.form: Currently, the best option IS BEING EVALUATED.
rows.example: Present Continuous Passive — right now.

rows.form: A decision WILL BE MADE by December.
rows.example: Future Passive — planned future.

rows.form: After the decision, implementation CAN BE STARTED.
rows.example: Modal Passive — after condition is met.

rows.form: If all goes well, the issue WILL HAVE BEEN RESOLVED by spring.
rows.example: Future Perfect Passive — by a future point.

grammarTip:
Passive — все формы:

PS: is/are + pp ("is collected")
PC: is/are being + pp ("is being reviewed")
PPS: has/have been + pp ("has been approved")
Past S: was/were + pp ("was introduced")
Past C: was/were being + pp ("was being processed")
Past Perf: had been + pp ("had been tested")
Future: will be + pp ("will be announced")
Modal: modal + be + pp ("must be checked")

GET PASSIVE (informal):
get/got/getting + pp
"She got fired." / "It's getting fixed."
→ Emphasises subject's EXPERIENCE
→ NOT used in academic/formal writing

BY + agent:
✅ Include when agent is important/surprising
✅ Omit when obvious or unknown

exercises.text: "Results ___ every Monday by the committee."
exercises.hint: "Results" = plural → ARE. Present Simple Passive: "Results ARE PUBLISHED every Monday." ✅

exercises.text: "The new platform ___ by three vendors right now."
exercises.hint: "Right now" = ongoing → Present Continuous Passive. "IS BEING EVALUATED." ✅

exercises.text: "The proposal ___ (review) and ___ (approve) by the committee."
exercises.correct: has been reviewed / has been approved
exercises.hint: Present Perfect Passive: "HAS BEEN REVIEWED and HAS BEEN APPROVED." ✅

exercises.text: "Penicillin ___ by Fleming in 1928."
exercises.hint: "In 1928" = specific past → Past Simple Passive. "WAS DISCOVERED." ✅

exercises.text: "The samples ___ when the power cut happened."
exercises.hint: Ongoing action interrupted by another → Past Continuous Passive. "WERE BEING PROCESSED when..." ✅

exercises.text: "The policy ___ (implement) before anyone noticed the error."
exercises.hint: Earlier past → Past Perfect Passive. "HAD BEEN IMPLEMENTED before..." ✅

exercises.text: "The final decision ___ at the next meeting in February."
exercises.hint: Future → WILL BE ANNOUNCED. "The decision WILL BE ANNOUNCED at the next meeting." ✅

exercises.text: "All submissions ___ before they are shared with staff."
exercises.hint: Modal passive (obligation): "MUST BE ANONYMISED." ✅

exercises.text: "The equipment ___ last week and still isn't working." (informal, experiential)
exercises.hint: "GET passive" past: "GOT BROKEN." Emphasises the equipment's experience of breaking. Informal. ✅

exercises.text: "Don't worry — your application ___ processed as we speak." (informal)
exercises.hint: "is being processed" (formal) ✅ / "is getting processed" (informal get passive) ✅ — both correct. ✅

exercises.text: "The Eiffel Tower was built ___ Gustave Eiffel." — Include "by"?
opts: Yes — Eiffel is important and adds information
exercises.correct: Yes — Eiffel is important and adds information
exercises.hint: "By Gustave Eiffel" = important! Who designed it IS the interesting information. Include BY + agent. ✅

exercises.text: "The report was wrote by the committee."
exercises.hint: ✅ "The report was WRITTEN by the committee." — PAST PARTICIPLE, not past simple! ✅

exercises.text: "The equation was being understood by all students."
opts: Wrong — stative verbs cannot be Continuous passive; should be "was understood"
exercises.correct: Wrong — stative verbs cannot be Continuous passive; should be "was understood"
exercises.hint: "understand" = stative → cannot use Continuous. ✅ "The equation WAS UNDERSTOOD by all students." ✅

exercises.text: "By the end of the project, all data will have been collected." — Tense: ___ Passive.
exercises.hint: "will have been collected" = will have + been + pp = FUTURE PERFECT PASSIVE. ✅

exercises.instruction: GET passive vs BE passive: which is MORE appropriate in an academic report?
exercises.text: "Three candidates were selected / got selected for interview."
opts: "Were selected" is more formal and appropriate for academic
exercises.correct: "Were selected" is more formal and appropriate for academic
exercises.hint: "GET passive" is informal — not appropriate in academic reports. "WERE SELECTED" ✅ is the correct academic form. ✅

exercises.instruction: Which passive shows an action ongoing at a past moment?
exercises.text: Which tense is needed: "The samples ___ when the power failed."
exercises.hint: Ongoing at past moment = PAST CONTINUOUS PASSIVE. "WERE BEING PROCESSED when the power failed." ✅

exercises.text: "The problem ___ (identify) last year. Since then, solutions ___ (propose). Currently, the best option ___ (evaluate)."
exercises.correct: was identified / have been proposed / is being evaluated
exercises.hint: PS Passive → PPS Passive → PC Passive. "WAS IDENTIFIED / HAVE BEEN PROPOSED / IS BEING EVALUATED." ✅

exercises.text: "The lab was cleaned ___ the technicians." — Should you include "by the technicians"?
opts: Probably no — the agent is obvious and adds no new information
exercises.correct: Probably no — the agent is obvious and adds no new information
exercises.hint: Obvious agent (technicians clean labs — expected) → OMIT "by the technicians." ✅

exercises.text: "By next June, the new system ___ fully."
exercises.hint: "By next June" = completed by a future point → Future Perfect Passive. "WILL HAVE BEEN IMPLEMENTED." ✅

exercises.text: "The files ___ (not / back up) when the computer crashed." (Past Perfect Passive, negative)
exercises.hint: Earlier past + negative → "HADN'T BEEN BACKED UP when the computer crashed." ✅

questions.hint: "is being revised" = is/are + being + pp = Present Continuous Passive. ✅

questions.text: "The error had been noticed before the report was finalised." — "had been noticed" is:
questions.hint: "had been noticed" = had + been + pp = Past Perfect Passive. Earlier past action. ✅

questions.text: "She got promoted." — What is special about "get passive" here?
opts: It emphasises her experience of being promoted
questions.correct: It emphasises her experience of being promoted
questions.hint: "Get passive emphasises the subject's experience." "Got promoted" feels more personal than "was promoted." ✅

questions.text: "The data was being collected when the error occurred." — Two tenses:
questions.hint: "was being collected" = PC Passive (ongoing background) + "occurred" = PS (interruption). ✅

questions.text: Which does NOT need BY + agent?
opts: "The Mona Lisa was painted by Leonardo." (important)
"The building was designed by a student." (surprising)
questions.hint: Obvious agent → OMIT by + agent. "The road was repaired." (no need to say "by workers") ✅

questions.text: "The solution was being understood by everyone." — What is wrong?
opts: "understand" is stative — cannot use Continuous passive; should be "was understood"
questions.correct: "understand" is stative — cannot use Continuous passive; should be "was understood"
questions.hint: Stative verbs cannot be Continuous. "The solution WAS UNDERSTOOD by everyone." ✅
"Get passive" = informal. Not used in academic essays, formal reports, or legal documents. ✅

questions.text: "By spring, the system ___ (fully / implement)." (Future Perfect Passive)
questions.hint: Future Perfect Passive: "WILL HAVE BEEN FULLY IMPLEMENTED." ✅

questions.text: "Three samples are collected daily." — Can you say "are being collected daily"?
opts: No difference; both correct for routine
"Are collected" = routine/scheduled; "are being collected" = right now/specifically
questions.correct: "Are collected" = routine/scheduled; "are being collected" = right now/specifically
questions.hint: PS Passive = routine/habitual. PC Passive = specifically happening right now. Different meaning! ✅

questions.text: "The report was wrote by the team." — Error:
questions.hint: ✅ "The report was WRITTEN." Past participle of "write" = "written." Never "wrote" in passive! ✅

questions.text: Which sentence is passive AND contextually appropriate?
opts: "The presentation got done in time." (informal context)
"She was being known as an expert." (stative)
questions.correct: "The presentation got done in time." (informal context)
questions.hint: "The presentation got done in time." = GET passive, informal, natural. ✅ All others have errors.
